chunks: Shuʿayb narrated from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdِ اللَّهِ عليه السلام, that he mentioned:

That ʿAlī عليه السلام was approached by a people disputing over a mule. Evidence was established for these people that they had bred it at their feeding trough, and they had neither sold it nor gifted it; and evidence was established for those people that they had bred it at their feeding trough, and they had neither sold it nor gifted it. So he عليه السلام ruled for the side with the greater evidence and made them swear an oath.

key_terms.بَغْلَةٍ: a mule, the disputed property in the case
key_terms.بَيِّنَةً: evidence, here meaning stronger or more numerous proof
key_terms.مِذْوَدِهِمْ: their feeding trough, indicating place of raising the animal
key_terms.وَاسْتَحْلَفَهُمْ: he required them to take an oath
key_terms.يَخْتَصِمُونَ: they were disputing or litigating a claim

ai.seo_question: How did Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام judge when both parties brought evidence in a property dispute?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a judicial ruling of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام in a property dispute where both sides produced evidence. He ruled in favor of the party with the greater number of witnesses and also required an oath, showing principles of adjudication in contested claims.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3344 - It is narrated by Shu'ayb from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdullah (as), that he mentioned:

A group of people came to Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as), disputing ownership of a mule. Both parties presented evidence.
One group claimed that they had raised it at their feeding trough, had neither sold it nor gifted it, and provided witnesses to support their claim.
The other group also claimed that they had raised it at their feeding trough, had neither sold it nor gifted it, and provided their own witnesses.
Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) ruled in favor of the group that had a greater number of witnesses and required them to take an oath to support their claim.
